questions.q: Whom did King Solomon love?
questions.a: King Solomon loved many foreign women.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command about marrying women from foreign nations?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded Israel not to marry women from foreign nations.

questions.q: What did Solomon’s wives do to his heart?
questions.a: Solomon’s wives turned his heart away from God, worshiping foreign gods.

questions.q: How was David’s heart toward Yahweh?
questions.a: David’s heart was completely faithful to Yahweh his God.

questions.q: What did Solomon follow?
questions.a: Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the disgusting god of the Ammonites.

questions.q: What did Solomon do in the sight of Yahweh?
questions.a: Solomon did that which was evil in the sight of Yahweh.

questions.q: What did Solomon build for Chemosh?
questions.a: Solomon built a shrine for Chemosh, the idol of Moab.

questions.q: What did Solomon do at the shrines of his foreign wives?
questions.a: Solomon burned incense and sacrificed to their gods at the shrines.

questions.q: How many times did Yahweh appear to Solomon?
questions.a: Yahweh appeared twice to Solomon.

questions.q: What did Yahweh command Solomon?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded Solomon not to go after foreign gods.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Solomon he would do because of the foreign gods?
questions.a: Yahweh told Solomon he would tear the kingdom from him and give it to his servant.

questions.q: How many tribes did Yahweh promise to give to Solomon’s son?
questions.a: Yahweh promised to give one tribe to Solomon’s son.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh raise up as an adversary to Solomon?
questions.a: Yahweh raised up Hadad the Edomite as an adversary to Solomon.

questions.q: Who went up to bury the dead who had been killed in Edom?
questions.a: Joab, the commander of the army, went up to bury the dead who were killed in Edom.

questions.q: How long did Joab and Israel remain in Edom?
questions.a: Joab and Israel remained in Edom six months.

questions.q: To where was Hadad taken?
questions.a: Hadad was taken to Egypt.

questions.q: Whom did Pharaoh give as a wife to Hadad?
questions.a: Pharaoh gave to Hadad the sister of Queen Tahpenes as his wife.

questions.q: What was the name of Hadad’s son?
questions.a: Hadad’s son was named Genubath.

questions.q: What did Hadad ask of Pharaoh?
questions.a: Hadad asked Pharaoh if he might depart and go to his own country.

questions.q: What was the name of another adversary that God raised up against Solomon?
questions.a: God raised up another adversary to Solomon named Rezon, the son of Eliada.

questions.q: To where did Rezon’s men travel?
questions.a: Rezon’s men went to Damascus and lived there.

questions.q: How long was Rezon an enemy of Israel?
questions.a: Rezon was an enemy of Israel all of the days of Solomon.

questions.q: Who else rebelled against the king?
questions.a: Jeroboam the son of Nebat also rebelled against King Solomon.

questions.q: Why did Jeroboam raise his hand against the king?
questions.a: Jeroboam the son of Nebat raised his hand against the king because the prophet Ahijah told him he would become king of ten tribes.

questions.q: What did Solomon give Jeroboam command over?
questions.a: Solomon gave Jeroboam command over all the labor of the house of Joseph.

questions.q: Who found Jeroboam in the road as he went out of Jerusalem?
questions.a: The prophet Ahijah found Jeroboam in the road as he went out of Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did Ahijah do to his new garment?
questions.a: Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say about Solomon’s kingdom?
questions.a: Yahweh said that he would tear the kingdom out of Solomon’s hand, giving ten tribes to Jeroboam.

questions.q: How many tribes would Solomon keep?
questions.a: Solomon would keep one tribe for the sake of David.

questions.q: How long did Yahweh make Solomon to be ruler?
questions.a: Yahweh made Solomon ruler all the days of his life.

questions.q: In which city did Yahweh choose to put his name?
questions.a: Yahweh chose to put his name in the city of Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did Yahweh promise to do for Jeroboam if he walked in his ways?
questions.a: Yahweh promised to be with him and give him an established house if Jeroboam walked in his ways.

questions.q: What did Solomon try to do to Jeroboam?
questions.a: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam.

questions.q: How long did Solomon reign in Jerusalem?
questions.a: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem for 40 years.

questions.q: Who became king in Solomon’s place?
questions.a: Rehoboam became king in Solomon’s place.

commentary.text: Solomon's wives and concubines, His idolatry.

Verses 1–8 There is not a more melancholy and astonishing instance of human depravity in the sacred Scriptures, than that here recorded. Solomon became a public worshipper of abominable idols! Probably he by degrees gave way to pride and luxury, and thus lost his relish for true wisdom. Nothing forms in itself a security against the deceitfulness and depravity of the human heart. Nor will old age cure the heart of any evil propensity. If our sinful passions are not crucified and mortified by the grace of God, they never will die of themselves, but will last even when opportunities to gratify them are taken away. Let him that thinks he stands, take heed lest he fall. We see how weak we are of ourselves, without the grace of God; let us therefore live in constant dependence on that grace. Let us watch and be sober: ours is a dangerous warfare, and in an enemy's country, while our worst foes are the traitors in our own hearts. (1Ki 11:9-13)

The Lord told Solomon, it is likely by a prophet, what he must expect for his apostacy. Though we have reason to hope that he repented, and found mercy, yet the Holy Ghost did not expressly record it, but left it doubtful, as a warning to others not to sin. The guilt may be taken away, but not the reproach; that will remain. Thus it must remain uncertain to us till the day of judgment, whether or not Solomon was left to suffer the everlasting displeasure of an offended God.

While Solomon kept close to God and to his duty, there was no enemy to give him uneasiness; but here we have an account of two. If against us, he can make us fear even the least, and the very grasshopper shall be a burden. Though they were moved by principles of ambition or revenge, God used them to correct Solomon.

In telling the reason why God rent the kingdom from the house of Solomon, Ahijah warned Jeroboam to take heed of sinning away his preferment. Yet the house of David must be supported; out of it the Messiah would arise. Solomon sought to kill his successor. Had not he taught others, that whatever devices are in men's hearts, the counsel of the Lord shall stand? Yet he himself thinks to defeat that counsel. Jeroboam withdrew into Egypt, and was content to live in exile and obscurity for awhile, being sure of a kingdom at last. Shall not we be content, who have a better kingdom in reserve?

Solomon's reign was as long as his father's, but his life was not so. Sin shortened his days. If the world, with all its advantages, could satisfy the soul, and afford real joy, Solomon would have found it so. But he was disappointed in all, and to warn us, has left this record of all earthly enjoyments, “Vanity and vexation of spirit.” The New Testament declares that one greater than Solomon is come to reign over us, and to possess the throne of his father David. May we not see something of Christ's excellency faintly represented to us in this figure?
